slots.node01.label: Today
slots.node01.title: A close that waits
slots.node02.text: Close takes 12 days, and about seven of them are spent waiting. Balance-sheet accounts are reconciled after the month ends, eleven entities match intercompany balances by email, and controllers see most entries for the first time on day nine. Errors surface when they are most expensive to fix, and every late finding reopens work that was already signed off.
slots.node03.text: The calendar looks full, but most of it is waiting: for a reconciliation, for a match, for a reviewer.
slots.node04.label: Target state
slots.node04.title: A close that flows
slots.node05.text: Reconciliations happen during the month, intercompany balances match overnight, and review rules check entries as they post. Exceptions reach a named owner on day one, so the days at the end are for sign-off rather than discovery. The controller signs off on day five, and the finance team gets its calendar back.
slots.node06.text: The calendar gets shorter because the waiting is designed out, not because anyone works faster.
slots.title: The close moves from waiting to flowing
